readerTitle: A great product you only use once a year
caseNote: 실제 관찰 (세금 신고, 이사, 결혼) + 가상 사례 (웨딩플래너, 세무 사무소, 식료품점)
insight: 좋은 리텐션은 매일 오는 것이 아니라, 문제가 다시 생길 때 다시 오는 것이다.
misconception: 좋은 사업이라면 고객이 자주 와야 한다. 방문 빈도가 모든 사업의 건강 지표다.

sources.text: 제품 분석 실무의 일반 개념 (단일 1차 출처 없음, 편집자 해석)

factChecks.note: 이 레슨은 특정 기업 사례 없이 일상 관찰과 가상 사례로만 구성했습니다. 앱 대신 웨딩플래너, 세무 사무소, 식료품점처럼 업종을 가리지 않는 사업을 썼습니다. 카드에 "Illustrative example" 표시를 붙였습니다.
"Natural usage frequency"는 제품 실무에서 널리 쓰는 표현이지만 하나의 정해진 1차 출처는 없습니다. 개념 설명은 편집자의 해석으로 표기합니다.
세금 신고 시즌 같은 국가별 일정은 예시로만 쓰고, 특정 국가의 세무 정보는 넣지 않았습니다.

cards.title: A great product you only use once a year
body: Think about the last time you hired movers, filed taxes or booked a wedding venue.
If those services were great, would you use them more often? Probably not. And that's fine.

image.label: A calendar with a single circled day
image.brief: 1년 달력 일러스트. 1년에 단 하루만 동그라미가 쳐져 있고, 그날 위에 이삿짐 상자·세금 서류·웨딩 케이크 아이콘이 작게 겹쳐 있음.

cards.title: Your partner wants more repeat business.
body: You run a wedding-planning business. Couples love you, but each couple needs you once.
Your business partner wants to add a monthly membership so clients keep paying after the wedding. What do you do?

options.text: Launch a monthly membership for married couples
options.feedback: Few couples need wedding help after the wedding. You'd spend effort selling something nobody needs and annoy the people who love you.

options.text: Measure success per wedding and grow through referrals and partner vendors
options.feedback: Every happy couple knows the next couple to get engaged, and venues and florists see dozens of couples a year. That's your growth loop.

options.text: Switch to all kinds of events: birthdays, parties, reunions
options.feedback: Maybe someday. For now you'd blur what you're known for to chase repeat visits that never fit wedding planning.

cards.title: Natural usage frequency
body: Every problem has a **natural frequency**: how often it actually comes up in a customer's life.
Messaging happens many times a day. Grocery shopping, about weekly. Taxes, yearly. A wedding, ideally once.
A product can't be used more often than its problem occurs. **Good retention means coming back when the problem comes back.**

image.label: Frequency ladder: daily → weekly → yearly → once
image.brief: 세로 사다리 인포그래픽. 위에서부터 "Messaging · many times a day", "Groceries · weekly", "Taxes · yearly", "Wedding · ideally once". 각 칸에 작은 아이콘.

cards.title: Visits per week is the wrong ruler for most businesses.
body: A tax-preparation practice that sees almost no clients in July is healthy. One that loses half its clients by the next tax season is in trouble.
So measure return visits at the natural interval: weekly for groceries, yearly for taxes, once per event for weddings or moves.
cards.softwareNote: This is why daily active users is the wrong goal for many apps. A travel-booking or tax app should track whether people come back at their natural interval, not every day.

cards.title: Grow without forcing frequency.
list: **Make each use excellent.** Rare products live on memory and reputation.
**Earn referrals.** Once-a-year customers know other people with the same problem.
**Be remembered at the right time.** A reminder before tax season helps. One every day doesn't.
**Help with the next job.** Movers can help with cleaning or storage, which come up at the same time.

cards.title: Sometimes low use really is a problem.
body: Natural frequency isn't an excuse. If regulars shop at your grocery store once a month, that's below the natural rhythm, and something is wrong.
Compare how often people use you with how often the problem happens. Falling below that rhythm is a warning. Pushing far above it usually creates annoyance, not value.

cards.title: Pick the right health check.
body: You run a tax-preparation practice. Which number best tells you whether clients are happy?

options.text: How often clients contact you during the year
options.feedback: Most clients only need you at tax time. Few calls in between can mean you did the job well.

options.text: Share of last year's clients who come back this year
options.feedback: Yes. It measures return at the natural rhythm, and it's what pays the bills next year.
More hours could mean messy records or confusion. Clients usually want it done quickly and correctly.

cards.title: Match your metrics to your customer's life, not your dashboard.
body: Ask how often the problem really happens. Measure and design around that rhythm.
**Try it today:** write down how often your customer's problem actually comes up. Is your main metric measured at that same rhythm?
